  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
      cfg='{}'
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
      prof='{}'
    fi
  else
    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
  fi
  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
        else . end)) as $knobs |
    {
      schema_version: 1,
      id: $id,
      profile: $sel.name,
      profile_source: $sel.source,
      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
      profile_keys: $keys,
      knobs: $knobs,
      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
  local w
  while IFS= read -r w; do
    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
  return 0
}

_loa_pl_write_cache() {
  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  fi
  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  else
    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
  fi
  return 0
}

        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
          _hd_full=1
          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
          _hd_full=1
        fi
      fi
      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
    done

}

# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
    start=0 pipe=0
    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
      # segment [start, j)
      own=0
      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
      if (( ! own )); then
        seg_has=0 cw=""
        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
        done
        if (( seg_has )); then
          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
          cw="$_hd_w"
          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
        fi
      fi
      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
      start=$((j + 1))
    done
  done
  return 1
}

# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
  _bdb_hd_class=none
  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
  text="${text%$'\n'}"
  _bdb_hd_L=()
  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
  i=0
  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
      out="$out$l"$'\n'
      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
      out="$out$l"$'\n'
      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
      i=$((i + 1)); continue
    fi
    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
    found=-1
    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
    done
    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
    cls="$_hd_cls"
    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
    fi
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
      local -a dests
      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
          cls=interpreter; break
        fi
      done
    fi
    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
    out="$out$l"$'\n'
    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
        out="$out$_hd_kept"
      fi
    else
      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
      out="$out$_hd_synth"
    fi
    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
    case "$cls" in
      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
    esac
    i=$((found + 1))
  done
  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
}

# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
}

# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r l; do
    case "$l" in
      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
    esac
    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
    fi
  done <<< "$content"
  return 0
}

# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
  local LC_ALL=C
  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
}
heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
  return 0
fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
     4	# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
     5	#
     6	# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
     7	# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
     8	# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
     9	# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
    10	# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
    11	# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
    12	# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
    13	# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
    14	# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
    15	# =============================================================================
    16	
    17	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
    18	
    19	setup() {
    20	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    21	    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    22	    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    23	    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    24	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    25	    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
    26	    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
    27	    for p in lean standard; do
    28	        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
    29	        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
    30	    done
    31	    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
    32	}
    33	
    34	# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
    35	floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }
    36	
    37	@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
    38	    local pin actual
    39	    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
    40	    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
    41	    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    42	    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
    43	}
    44	
    45	@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
    46	    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
    47	import re, subprocess, sys, json
    48	def load(p):
    49	    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
    50	prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
    51	keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
    52	assert len(keys) == 9, keys
    53	bad = []
    54	for k in keys:
    55	    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
    56	        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
    57	        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
    58	            bad.append((k, f))
    59	print("violations:", bad)
    60	sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
    61	PY
    62	    echo "$output"
    63	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    64	    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
    65	    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    66	}
    67	
    68	@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
    69	    local p k
    70	    for p in lean standard; do
    71	        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
    72	        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
    73	    done
    74	    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a
    75	    # floor pattern matches (flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice expands here).
    76	    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml" > "$T/cfg.json"
    77	    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" > "$T/ex.json"
    78	    floor_keys > "$T/floor.txt"
    79	    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
    80	import json, re, sys
    81	pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
    82	rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
    83	out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
    84	def walk(x, path):
    85	    if isinstance(x, dict):
    86	        for k, v in x.items():
    87	            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
    88	    if path:
    89	        key = ".".join(path)
    90	        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
    91	            out.add(key)
    92	for f in sys.argv[1:3]:
    93	    walk(json.load(open(f)), [])
    94	print("\n".join(sorted(k for k in out if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*", k))))
    95	PY
    96	    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
    97	    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
    98	    grep -q '^flatline_protocol\.[a-z_]*\.companion_voice$' "$T/concrete.txt"
    99	    while IFS= read -r k; do
   100	        [ "$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.knobs | has($k)' "$T/lean.json")" = "false" ] || { echo "lean resolves floor key $k"; return 1; }
   101	        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
   102	        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
   103	        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
   104	    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
   105	    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
   106	    for g in code_review security_audit; do
   107	        cmp <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/lean.yaml") <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/standard.yaml")
   108	    done
   109	}
   110	
   111	@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {
   112	    local f p
   113	    printf 'All good\n\n## Observations\n\n- **LOW** `a.sh:1` — naming\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":1},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/ok.md"
   114	    printf '## Changes Required\n\n- **HIGH** `a.sh:1` — unchecked input\n\nAll good\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/bad.md"
   115	    for f in ok bad; do
   116	        for p in lean standard; do
   117	            rc=0
   118	            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$R/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$T/$f.md" --gate review --json \
   119	                > "$T/vd-$f-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   120	            echo "$rc" >> "$T/vd-$f-$p.out"
   121	        done
   122	        cmp "$T/vd-$f-lean.out" "$T/vd-$f-standard.out"
   123	    done

   125	    ! cmp -s "$T/vd-ok-lean.out" "$T/vd-bad-lean.out"
   126	}
   127	
   128	@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {
   129	    local d="$T/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-999" p rc
   130	    mkdir -p "$d"

   132	        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled = true' "$T/$p.yaml"
   133	        rc=0
   134	        printf '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/COMPLETED"}}' "$d" \
   135	            | env -u LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_CONFIG_PATH_OVERRIDE="$T/$p.yaml" \
   136	              bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" > "$T/gate-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   137	        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"
   138	    done

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats

     6	# `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds the run position from files: one case per
     7	# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
     8	# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
     9	# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
    10	# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
    11	# =============================================================================

    14	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"

    16	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcd.XXXXXX")"
    17	  R="$T/repo"
    18	  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a" "$R/.run" "$R/src"
    19	  git -C "$R" init -q
    20	  printf 'x\n' > "$R/src/a.ts"
    21	  git -C "$R" add -A
    22	  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm "feat: impl"
    23	  ledger completed completed completed

    25	}
    26	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    27	
    28	# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
    29	ledger() {
    30	  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
    31	    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
    32	     cycles: [
    33	       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    34	        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
    35	       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    36	        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    37	                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    38	                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
    39	                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    40	}
    41	
    42	# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
    43	feedback() {
    44	  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
    45	  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"

    49	    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    50	  else
    51	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
    52	  fi
    53	  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
    54	    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
    55	}
    56	
    57	# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
    58	complete() {

    60	  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"

    62	}

    70	               list: [{id: "sprint-1", status: "in_progress"}, {id: "sprint-2", status: "pending"}, {id: "sprint-3", status: "pending"}]}}
    71	    '"${3:+| $3}" > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    72	}

    74	derive() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
     5	# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
     6	# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
     7	# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
     8	# All files live in a temp dir.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    13	  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
    14	  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
    16	  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
    17	  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
    18	  S="$T/.run/state.json"
    19	  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
    20	}
    21	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    22	
    23	# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
    24	fb() {
    25	  local prose
    26	  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
    27	    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    28	  else
    29	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
    30	  fi
    31	  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
    32	    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
    33	}
    34	
    35	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
    36	
    37	breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
    38	  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
    39	          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
    40	                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
    41	          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
    42	}

    44	rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }
    45	
    46	@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {

    49	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    50	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    51	  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
    52	  local want
    53	  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
    54	  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
    55	  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
    56	  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
    57	}
    58	
    59	@test "RCR-2 the same hash again counts up; a different finding set resets same_issue to 1 with the new last_hash" {
    60	  breaker

    63	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    64	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 2 ]
    65	  local h1; h1=$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")
    66	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 2

    81	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 2 ]
    82	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 3

    85	}

    96	  run jq -r '[.state, (.history | length), .history[0].trigger, .history[0].gate, .history[0].sprint] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
    97	  [ "$output" = "OPEN 1 same_issue audit sprint-1" ]

   100	  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"

   103	}

   106	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
   107	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 19'
   108	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
   109	  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]

   111	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = "{\"critical\":0,\"high\":0,\"medium\":1,\"low\":0}"'
   112	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
   113	  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
   114	  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: no_progress: "* ]]
   115	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.timeout.started = (now - 9 * 3600 | floor | todate)'
   116	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy enforcement v1
     3	# (#961 K-1 / FR-1)
     4	#
     5	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Reads tool_input JSON from stdin,
     6	# accumulates session diff lines at .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl, and emits
     7	# a `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line + trajectory event when the running
     8	# total exceeds `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100).
     9	#
    10	# Non-blocking by design — returns 0 regardless. The `enforce: block` config
    11	# semantic is RESERVED for v2; v1 honors `warn` only to avoid surprise breakage
    12	# during initial rollout. See grimoires/loa/sdd.md §3.3 + §7 R-3.
    13	#
    14	# Safety invariants (NFR-Sec-1):
    15	#   - tool_input.content / tool_input.new_string NEVER written to state or
    16	#     trajectory. Only line counts + file paths are recorded.
    17	#   - file_path is JSON-escaped inside jq (tojson — the same encoder the old
    18	#     `jq --arg` path used) — no shell-injection vector.
    19	#   - Hook MUST exit 0 even when yq/jq are missing or config is malformed
    20	#     (graceful degradation; never break Write/Edit due to hook env issues).
    21	#
    22	# perf pass-3 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): jq/yq single-pass consolidation.
    23	# Was (warn regime, the production steady state): yq x2 + jq x7 + wc x2 +
    24	# tr x2 + cat + date x3 + awk. Now: yq x1 + jq x1 + awk + mkdir/dirname.
    25	# Design + isomorphism notes:
    26	#   - ONE yq derives two guaranteed-single-line decision tokens: (1) whether
    27	#     the master switch renders as an explicit false-equivalent (the same
    28	#     ten-token list the old bash `case` matched against the $()-stripped
    29	#     rendering — tostring + sub("\n+$";"") reproduces that stripping), and
    30	#     (2) the threshold rendering when it matches ^[0-9]+$, else "DEFAULT"
    31	#     (the old bash regex guard, applied inside yq so multi-line values
    32	#     cannot pollute line-based token reads). A grep-style "config lacks the
    33	#     key" pre-check was REJECTED: YAML double-quoted keys can be spelled
    34	#     with escape sequences, so textual absence does not prove key absence.
    35	#   - ONE jq (slurp) replaces: `jq empty` validation, tool_name extraction,
    36	#     the content/new_string line count (jq|wc -l|tr), file_path extraction,
    37	#     the files_modified jq -rs aggregation and the wc -l tool_call_count.
    38	#     Line counts replicate `jq -r ... | wc -l` byte semantics exactly:
    39	#     strings count split("\n") segments (empty string = 1, matching the
    40	#     old raw-output trailing newline), null/false vanish via `// empty`
    41	#     (0), other scalars are 1 line, and containers use a recursive
    42	#     pretty-print line-count (def jl) that matches jq's pretty renderer
    43	#     (host-verified against wc -l on nested fixtures).
    44	#   - files_modified/tool_call_count are computed analytically PRE-append
    45	#     ([state files] + current file | unique; NL-count + 1) — provably equal
    46	#     to the old POST-append `jq -rs`/`wc -l` reads for every hook-written
    47	#     state file, including the unterminated-final-line case. The jq -rs
    48	#     wholesale-failure semantic (ANY malformed state line -> 0) is
    49	#     replicated with a try/catch around a per-line fromjson parse.
    50	#     (Out-of-contract shapes an external writer could create — multi-line
    51	#     pretty JSON docs or whitespace-only lines — count as malformed here
    52	#     where the old stream parser tolerated them; state is hook-written.)
    53	#   - The state line and trajectory event are printf-assembled from
    54	#     jq-pre-encoded pieces (tojson == the old jq -nc --arg encoder, key
    55	#     order preserved) — byte-identical output, zero builder spawns.
    56	#   - Timestamps: now|todate == date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ (host-verified);
    57	#     the trajectory filename date is the timestamp's date field (single
    58	#     clock read — removes a midnight-straddle inconsistency, same as the
    59	#     pass-2 zone-guard change). The session-id date (LOA_SESSION_ID unset)
    60	#     uses gmtime|strftime("%Y%m%d") — same UTC day.
    61	#   - Field transport is NUL-delimited ("[0] | implode" builds the NUL;
    62	#     no escape literal appears in this file): file paths and tool names
    63	#     can contain tabs/newlines, which @tsv would rewrite. Embedded JSON
    64	#     NUL escapes (backslash-u-0000) are stripped via string division AND
    65	#     trailing newlines are stripped (scap) — byte-identical to the old $()
    66	#     substitution (minus bash's cosmetic "ignored null byte" warning).
    67	#     Non-string tool_name/file_path values (out of hook contract) render
    68	#     via tojson (compact) where the old jq -r pretty-printed containers;
    69	#     scalars are byte-identical and every non-Write/Edit/NotebookEdit
    70	#     rendering exits 0 through the same case fall-through as before.
    71	#   - Error-shape parity: jq parse failure (invalid JSON stdin) exits 0
    72	#     exactly like the old `jq empty || exit 0`; a post-validation
    73	#     extraction error (e.g. non-object top-level doc) surfaces as an
    74	#     in-band __KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__ marker and exits 5, the code the old
    75	#     set -e death propagated from the failing extraction pipeline.
    76	#     Multi-document stdin (not producible by Claude Code) keeps the old
    77	#     concatenated-rendering semantics via slurp+join("\n").
    78	#
    79	# perf pass-4 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): redundant-spawn elimination — the
    80	# remaining dirname x2 + mkdir x2 drop out of the steady state: SCRIPT_DIR
    81	# uses the pass-2 parameter-expansion idiom; the state-dir mkdir is skipped
    82	# when a [[ -d ]] probe proves the parent exists (guard passing ⇒ dirname's
    83	# target exists ⇒ mkdir -p is a no-op; ANY other shape — no slash, trailing
    84	# slash, missing parent — falls back to the old dirname+mkdir command
    85	# unchanged); the warn-path trajectory mkdir gets the same [[ -d ]] guard.
    86	# The running-total awk read was NOT merged into the jq pass (deliberate
    87	# skip): awk's tolerant textual parse counts lines_changed from lines that
    88	# are not valid JSON (e.g. a crash-truncated final line), which the jq
    89	# fromjson path cannot replicate without reimplementing strtod-prefix
    90	# numeric parsing — behavior on truncated state files would diverge.
    91	#
    92	# perf pass-6 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): memoization — the pass-3 two-token
    93	# yq derivation is a PURE function of the config file's bytes, re-derived on
    94	# EVERY Write/Edit. The token array is now cached at
    95	# .run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens (.run/ is State-Zone,
    96	# gitignored). Design notes:
    97	#   - Cache format: line 1 = key "<ns-mtime>:<size>:<abs-path>" of the
    98	#     config (ONE GNU-first `stat -Lc '%y:%s'` spawn — cheaper than the yq
    99	#     it replaces; non-GNU stat ⇒ no key ⇒ never cache, always parse);
   100	#     remaining lines = the _cfg_tokens array joined by newlines. %y is
   101	#     nanosecond mtime (same-second edits rotate the key); the abs-path
   102	#     component keeps two repos/worktrees sharing a relative
   103	#     LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE name from cross-contaminating.
   104	#   - COLD path is the ORIGINAL procsub mapfile verbatim (byte-identical
   105	#     behavior including yq-failure partial output); the cache write is
   106	#     atomic ($$-temp + mv -f -T, same dir; readers see old or new file,
   107	#     never a torn one; concurrent writers: last wins) and any write
   108	#     failure is swallowed. WARM path reconstructs the exact token array;
   109	#     ANY anomaly (missing/corrupt/unreadable cache, key mismatch, stat
   110	#     failure) falls through to the cold path and rewrites the cache. An
   111	#     edit to the config is reflected in the very next invocation (key is
   112	#     stat'd BEFORE the parse — a racing write self-heals next call).
   113	#   - Token round-trip is exact for every yq-emittable stream here: both
   114	#     tokens are guaranteed single-line and non-empty by the yq program
   115	#     (bool literal / digits-or-DEFAULT). TRAILING empty tokens would not
   116	#     survive the $(<cache) trailing-newline strip — unreachable, and even
   117	#     if reached the downstream defaults coincide ("" and unset both yield
   118	#     THRESHOLD=100; "" != "true" for the switch either way). Mid-stream
   119	#     empty tokens round-trip exactly. Cached tokens are NUL-free by
   120	#     construction (bash variables cannot hold NUL).
   121	#   - Trust: config is already attacker-equivalent to the cache — anyone
   122	#     who can write .run/perf-cache/ can write .loa.config.yaml (same
   123	#     operator-writable trust domain), and this hook is non-blocking
   124	#     (warn-only) by design.
   125	#   - If the two-token yq program EVER changes, bump the cache filename
   126	#     version (v1 → v2). jq/yq availability checks stay unconditional so
   127	#     tool-absent behavior is unchanged.
   128	#
   129	# perf pass-7 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): O(n) -> O(delta/1) on the growing
   130	# state file via an incremental aggregate cache at
   131	# .run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg. FULL DESIGN NOTES are at the very
   132	# BOTTOM of this file, AFTER the final `exit 0` — bash never parses past an
   133	# executed exit, so the commentary costs zero runtime on the per-Write/Edit
   134	# hot path (measured ~0.35ms/KB of pre-exit comment lexing on this host).
   135	
   136	set -euo pipefail
   137	umask 077
   138	
   139	# perf pass-4: was $(cd "$(dirname BASH_SOURCE)" && pwd). ${p%/*} equals
   140	# dirname for every slash-containing script path; the two unreachable-in-
   141	# production shapes (bare filename via PATH-less invocation → ".", root-level
   142	# script "/x.sh" → "/") are covered explicitly. The cd/pwd canonicalization
   143	# subshell is retained. (Idiom copied from the pass-2 zone-write-guard.)
   144	_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
   145	_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
   146	if [[ "${_src_dir}" == "${_src}" ]]; then _src_dir="."; fi
   147	if [[ -z "${_src_dir}" ]]; then _src_dir="/"; fi
   148	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "${_src_dir}" && pwd)"
   149	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
   150	CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml}"
   151	TASK_STATE="${KARPATHY_TASK_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
   152	TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
   153	
   154	# Graceful degradation: missing tools or config → no-op.
   155	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
   156	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
   157	[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0
   158	
   159	# Fast-path: master switch off → no-op (<10ms target).
   160	# NOTE: yq's `// true` defaults trip on explicit `false` values (`false` is
   161	# treated as null by the alternative operator). Read raw, then test for the
   162	# specific false-equivalents (token 1). Token 2 carries the threshold.
   163	# perf pass-6: token array memoized keyed on config identity (header note);
   164	# any cache anomaly falls through to the original yq parse below.
   165	_KP_CACHE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens"
   166	_kp_src="$CONFIG"
   167	[[ "$_kp_src" != /* ]] && _kp_src="$PWD/$_kp_src"
   168	# perf pass-7: ONE stat now serves both the pass-6 config-cache key (%y:%s,
   169	# reassembled byte-identically from the %s/%y fields) and the pass-7
   170	# state-cache identity — the second stat spawn folds into the first. %n
   171	# prefixes each output line so a missing file cannot shift the mapping (GNU
   172	# stat keeps printing the surviving arguments after a failure). Pathological
   173	# '|'-bearing paths can only make a prefix-match miss or collide, leaving
   174	# fields empty/invalid = fail-open (no cache, original behavior).
   175	_kp7_st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%d|%i|%s|%y' -- "$CONFIG" "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) || true
   176	_kp_id=""
   177	_kp7_pre=""
   178	while IFS= read -r _kp7_l; do
   179	    case "$_kp7_l" in
   180	        "$CONFIG|"*)
   181	            IFS='|' read -r _kp7_cd _kp7_ci _kp7_cs _kp7_cy <<< "${_kp7_l#"$CONFIG|"}"
   182	            [[ -n "${_kp7_cy:-}" && -n "${_kp7_cs:-}" ]] && _kp_id="${_kp7_cy}:${_kp7_cs}"
   183	            ;;
   184	        "$TASK_STATE|"*)
   185	            _kp7_pre="${_kp7_l#"$TASK_STATE|"}"
   186	            ;;
   187	    esac
   188	done <<< "$_kp7_st"
   189	_kp_key=""
   190	[[ -n "$_kp_id" ]] && _kp_key="${_kp_id}:${_kp_src}"
   191	_cfg_tokens=()
   192	_kp_hit=0
   193	if [[ -n "$_kp_key" && -f "$_KP_CACHE_FILE" ]]; then
   194	    # Slurp via the read builtin, NOT $(<file): a failed $(<file) redirection
   195	    # aborts an errexit shell even inside a || list (host-probed, bash 5.2)
   196	    # and leaks a bash error line; read -rd '' returns empty on missing/
   197	    # unreadable/dir/NUL-torn inputs — exactly the fail-open we need — and
   198	    # preserves the file bytes verbatim ("<key>\n<tokens...>", the payload
   199	    # carrying no trailing newline by construction of the writer below; an
   200	    # empty payload means a validly-cached EMPTY token stream = yq failure).
   201	    _kp_cached=""
   202	    IFS= read -rd '' _kp_cached 2>/dev/null < "$_KP_CACHE_FILE" || true
   203	    if [[ "$_kp_cached" == "$_kp_key"$'\n'* ]]; then
   204	        _kp_payload="${_kp_cached#*$'\n'}"
   205	        [[ -n "$_kp_payload" ]] && mapfile -t _cfg_tokens <<< "$_kp_payload"
   206	        _kp_hit=1
   207	    fi
   208	fi
   209	if [[ "$_kp_hit" -eq 0 ]]; then
   210	    mapfile -t _cfg_tokens < <(
   211	        yq -r '(.karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning | tostring | sub("\n+$"; "") | (. == "false" or . == "False" or . == "FALSE" or . == "0" or . == "no" or . == "No" or . == "NO" or . == "off" or . == "Off" or . == "OFF")),
   212	               (.karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task | tostring | sub("\n+$"; "") | (with(select(test("^[0-9]+$") | not); . = "DEFAULT")))' \
   213	            "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null
   214	    )
   215	    if [[ -n "$_kp_key" ]]; then
   216	        _kp_payload=""
   217	        if [[ "${#_cfg_tokens[@]}" -gt 0 ]]; then
   218	            printf -v _kp_payload '%s\n' "${_cfg_tokens[@]}"
   219	            _kp_payload="${_kp_payload%$'\n'}"
   220	        fi
   221	        {
   222	            [[ -d "${_KP_CACHE_FILE%/*}" ]] || mkdir -p "${_KP_CACHE_FILE%/*}"
   223	            printf '%s\n%s' "$_kp_key" "$_kp_payload" > "$_KP_CACHE_FILE.$$" &&
   224	                mv -f -T "$_KP_CACHE_FILE.$$" "$_KP_CACHE_FILE"
   225	        } 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$_KP_CACHE_FILE.$$" 2>/dev/null || true
   226	    fi
   227	fi
   228	[[ "${_cfg_tokens[0]-}" == "true" ]] && exit 0
   229	
   230	THRESHOLD="${_cfg_tokens[1]-DEFAULT}"
   231	[[ "$THRESHOLD" == "null" || -z "$THRESHOLD" ]] && THRESHOLD=100
   232	# Validate threshold is a positive integer; default to 100 on parse failure.
   233	[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
   234	
   235	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   236	# perf pass-7: state-aggregate cache — mode decision (header note).
   237	# _kp7_blen: byte length of $1 into _kp7_len (locale-proof: ${#} counts
   238	# characters under multibyte locales; the local LC_ALL=C scope makes it
   239	# count bytes without disturbing the ambient locale of jq/awk children).
   240	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   241	_kp7_blen() { local LC_ALL=C; _kp7_len=${#1}; }
   242	
   243	_KP7_CACHE="$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg"
   244	# Size gate: below this many bytes the ORIGINAL full-scan path is already
   245	# cheaper than the cache machinery's fixed cost (warm jq compile + post-stat
   246	# + atomic mv ≈ 7ms vs ~4.7ms of scan per 1000 entries — measured crossover
   247	# ≈ 1300 entries ≈ 260KB, where the gate sits). Below the gate NO cache is
   248	# written; a valid existing cache is still honored — and since cache writes
   249	# only happen at ≥ gate, offset ≥ gate ⇒ any warm-eligible file is above the
   250	# gate too (no serve-without-write loop). The env override exists for the
   251	# test harness (do not mix gate values against one state file); same trust
   252	# class as KARPATHY_TASK_STATE (hook is warn-only, non-blocking).
   253	_KP7_MIN="${KARPATHY_STATE_CACHE_MIN:-262144}"
   254	[[ "$_KP7_MIN" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || _KP7_MIN=262144
   255	_kp7_mode="cold"        # cold | fast | delta
   256	_kp7_sum_mode="original" # original | fast | delta
   257	_kp7_write_ok=0          # may attempt a cache write post-append
   258	_kp7_warm=0              # 1 = primary fields sourced from the warm jq
   259	_kp7_dev=""; _kp7_ino=""; _kp7_s0=""; _kp7_mt=""
   260	_kp7_off=""; _kp7_bpois=""; _kp7_bnl=""; _kp7_bsum=""; _kp7_bcount=""
   261	_kp7_bset=""; _kp7_tok=""; _kp7_toklen=0; _kp7_tail_from=1
   262	_kp7_wcount=""; _kp7_snext=""; _kp7_pois2=""; _kp7_nls=""; _kp7_dlen=""
   263	_kp7_endsnl=""; _kp7_allstr=""
   264	_kp7_abs="$TASK_STATE"
   265	[[ "$_kp7_abs" != /* ]] && _kp7_abs="$PWD/$_kp7_abs"
   266	
   267	# awk/tail absence would make a FAST hit diverge from the old
   268	# `awk … || echo 0` fallback (cached sum vs 0) — disable the whole feature.
   269	if command -v awk >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v tail >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   270	    _kp7_write_ok=1
   271	    # _kp7_pre was captured by the combined stat above (config-cache block).
   272	    if [[ -n "$_kp7_pre" ]]; then
   273	        IFS='|' read -r _kp7_dev _kp7_ino _kp7_s0 _kp7_mt <<< "$_kp7_pre"
   274	    elif [[ -e "$TASK_STATE" ]]; then
   275	        _kp7_write_ok=0   # exists but stat failed (non-GNU stat) → fail open
   276	    else
   277	        _kp7_s0=0         # absent: cold with empty base; cacheable post-append
   278	    fi
   279	    if [[ "$_kp7_write_ok" -eq 1 && -n "$_kp7_dev" && -f "$TASK_STATE" && -r "$TASK_STATE" && -f "$_KP7_CACHE" ]]; then
   280	        # Nine line-reads from ONE fd (no herestring temp file; a concurrent
   281	        # cache mv cannot tear the read — the fd pins the inode). Line 9
   282	        # (the set) is slurped with read -rd '' and must contain no newline
   283	        # (exactly-9-lines shape check). Any read failure leaves fields
   284	        # empty and the validation below falls through to cold.
   285	        _kp7_c0=""; _kp7_c2=""; _kp7_c8=""
   286	        _kp7_off=""; _kp7_bpois=""; _kp7_bnl=""; _kp7_bsum=""
   287	        _kp7_bcount=""; _kp7_tok=""
   288	        {
   289	            IFS= read -r _kp7_c0 && IFS= read -r _kp7_off &&
   290	            IFS= read -r _kp7_c2 && IFS= read -r _kp7_bpois &&
   291	            IFS= read -r _kp7_bnl && IFS= read -r _kp7_bsum &&
   292	            IFS= read -r _kp7_bcount && IFS= read -r _kp7_tok &&
   293	            { IFS= read -rd '' _kp7_c8 || [[ -n "$_kp7_c8" ]]; }
   294	        } 2>/dev/null < "$_KP7_CACHE" || _kp7_c0=""
   295	        _kp7_bset="$_kp7_c8"
   296	        _kp7_blen "$_kp7_tok"; _kp7_toklen="$_kp7_len"

        ([0] | implode) as $z |
        try (
          (map(.tool_name // empty | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | join("\n") | scap($z)) as $tn |
          now as $now |
          ($sid | if . == "" then $user + "-" + ($now | gmtime | strftime("%Y%m%d")) else . end) as $session |
          (if $tn == "Write"
           then (map(.tool_input.content // empty) | map(if type == "string" then slines else jl end) | add // 0)
           elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit")
           then (map(.tool_input.new_string // empty) | map(if type == "string" then slines else jl end) | add // 0)
           else 0 end) as $lines |
          (if ($tn == "Write" or $tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit")
           then (map((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end)) | join("\n") | scap($z))
           else "" end) as $file |
          (if $fast == "1" then 0
           elif ($d | contains("�")) then 1
           elif (($d | startswith($tok + "\n")) | not) then 1
           else 0 end) as $anomA |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $fast == "1" then "" else $d[(($tok | length) + 1):] end) as $delta |
          ($delta | split("\n")) as $dsplit |
          (if $anomA == 1 then null
           else (try ($dsplit | map(select(length > 0) | fromjson) | [.[].file // empty]) catch null) end) as $dfiles |
          (if $anomA == 1 then 1 elif ($bpois == "1" or $dfiles == null) then 1 else 0 end) as $pois2 |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $pois2 == 1 then false
           elif ($dfiles | length) > 0 then false
           else (("," + ($bset | .[1:(length - 1)]) + ",")
                 | contains("," + ($file | tojson) + ",")) end) as $hit |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $pois2 == 1 or $hit then null
           else (try ($bset | fromjson) catch null) end) as $bs |
          (if $anomA == 1 or $pois2 == 1 or $hit then $anomA
           elif ($bs | type) != "array" then 1
           else $anomA end) as $anom |
          (if $anom == 1 or $pois2 == 1 or $hit then []
           else (($bs + $dfiles + [$file]) | unique) end) as $snext |
          (if $anom == 1 then "0"
           elif $pois2 == 1 then "0"
           elif $hit then $bcount
           else ($snext | length | tostring) end) as $files_mod |
          (if $anom == 1 then "0"
           elif $pois2 == 1 or $hit then $bcount
           else ($snext | length | tostring) end) as $count_next |
          (if $anom == 1 then ""
           elif $pois2 == 1 or $hit then "="
           else ($snext | tojson) end) as $setout |
          (if $anom == 1 then 0
           else (($bnl | tonumber)
                 + (if $delta == "" then 0 else (($dsplit | length) - 1) end)) end) as $nls |
          (if $anom == 1 then "0" else (($nls + 1) | tostring) end) as $tool_calls |
          ([$tn, ($lines | tostring), ($now | todate), ($file | tojson),
            ($session | tojson), $files_mod, $tool_calls,
            (if $anom == 1 then "1" else "0" end),
            $count_next,
            $setout,
            ($pois2 | tostring),
            ($nls | tostring),
            (if $anom == 1 then "0" else ($delta | utf8bytelength | tostring) end),
            (if $anom == 1 then "0" elif ($delta == "" or ($delta | endswith("\n"))) then "1" else "0" end),
            (if $anom == 1 then "0"
             elif $pois2 == 1 or $hit then "1"
             else (if ($snext | all(type == "string")) then "1" else "0" end) end)]
           | join($z) + $z)
        ) catch ("__KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__" + $z)
    '
    if [[ "$_kp7_mode" == "delta" ]]; then
        mapfile -d '' -t _kw < <(
            { _wrc=0
              jq -sj --rawfile d <(tail -c +"$_kp7_tail_from" -- "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) \
                 --arg fast "0" --arg tok "$_kp7_tok" --arg bset "$_kp7_bset" \
                 --arg bpois "$_kp7_bpois" --arg bnl "$_kp7_bnl" --arg bcount "$_kp7_bcount" \
                 --arg sid "${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}" --arg user "${USER:-unknown}" \
                 "$_KP7_WARM_PROG" 2>/dev/null || _wrc=$?
              printf '%s' "$_wrc"
            }
        )
    else
        mapfile -d '' -t _kw < <(
            { _wrc=0
              jq -sj --arg d "" \
                 --arg fast "1" --arg tok "$_kp7_tok" --arg bset "$_kp7_bset" \
                 --arg bpois "$_kp7_bpois" --arg bnl "$_kp7_bnl" --arg bcount "$_kp7_bcount" \
                 --arg sid "${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}" --arg user "${USER:-unknown}" \
                 "$_KP7_WARM_PROG" 2>/dev/null || _wrc=$?
              printf '%s' "$_wrc"
            }
        )
    fi
    [[ "${#_kw[@]}" -ge 1 ]] || exit 0
    # Invalid JSON on stdin — the old `jq empty 2>/dev/null || exit 0` path.
    [[ "${_kw[-1]}" == "0" ]] || exit 0
    # Post-validation extraction error — the old set -e death (exit 5). The
    # warm program's pre-payload bindings cannot error (bash-validated
    # inputs, try-wrapped parses), so this fires iff the original would.
    if [[ "${#_kw[@]}" -eq 2 && "${_kw[0]}" == "__KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__" ]]; then
        exit 5
    fi
    if [[ "${#_kw[@]}" -eq 16 && "${_kw[7]}" == "0" ]]; then
        TOOL_NAME="${_kw[0]}"
        LINES="${_kw[1]}"
        TS="${_kw[2]}"
        FILE_JSON="${_kw[3]}"
        SESSION_JSON="${_kw[4]}"
        FILES_MOD="${_kw[5]}"
        TOOL_CALLS="${_kw[6]}"
        _kp7_wcount="${_kw[8]}"; _kp7_snext="${_kw[9]}"; _kp7_pois2="${_kw[10]}"
        _kp7_nls="${_kw[11]}"; _kp7_dlen="${_kw[12]}"; _kp7_endsnl="${_kw[13]}"
        _kp7_allstr="${_kw[14]}"
        _kp7_warm=1
        _kp7_sum_mode="$_kp7_mode"
    elif [[ "${#_kw[@]}" -eq 16 ]]; then
        # Anomaly: full rescan. stdin is consumed, so keep the payload
        # fields (extracted with the original expressions) and recompute
        # the state aggregates PRE-append with the original expressions.
        TOOL_NAME="${_kw[0]}"
        LINES="${_kw[1]}"
        TS="${_kw[2]}"
        FILE_JSON="${_kw[3]}"
        SESSION_JSON="${_kw[4]}"
        _kp7_aux_state=(--arg state "")
        [[ -f "$TASK_STATE" && -r "$TASK_STATE" ]] && _kp7_aux_state=(--rawfile state "$TASK_STATE")
        mapfile -d '' -t _ka < <(
            { _arc=0
              jq -nj "${_kp7_aux_state[@]}" --arg fj "$FILE_JSON" '
                ([0] | implode) as $z |
                ($fj | fromjson) as $file |
                ((try ($state | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | fromjson)
                      | ([.[].file // empty] + [$file] | unique | length))
                  catch 0) | tostring) as $files_mod |
                ((if $state == "" then 1 else ($state | split("\n") | length) end) | tostring) as $tool_calls |
                ($files_mod + $z + $tool_calls + $z)
              ' 2>/dev/null || _arc=$?
              printf '%s' "$_arc"
            }
        )
        # A state re-read failure here matches the old shape: the original
        # single jq would have failed its --rawfile and exited 0 pre-append.
        [[ "${#_ka[@]}" -eq 3 && "${_ka[-1]}" == "0" ]] || exit 0
        FILES_MOD="${_ka[0]}"
        TOOL_CALLS="${_ka[1]}"
        _kp7_warm=1
        _kp7_sum_mode="original"
        _kp7_mode="cold"
    else
        # Defensive: unexpected field count (same class as the original
        # `-eq 8 || exit 0` guard).
        exit 0
    fi
fi

if [[ "$_kp7_warm" -eq 0 ]]; then
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # COLD path — the ORIGINAL single-jq code, verbatim (pass-3/4 shape).
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # ONE jq over stdin (+ the state file when present) — see header note.
    # Output stream: tn NUL lines NUL ts NUL file-json NUL session-json NUL
    # files-mod NUL tool-calls NUL, then the jq exit code as a final in-band
    # chunk (the procsub group neutralizes set -e around the jq).
    _state_args=(--arg state "")
    [[ -f "$TASK_STATE" && -r "$TASK_STATE" ]] && _state_args=(--rawfile state "$TASK_STATE")

    mapfile -d '' -t _kf < <(
        { _jrc=0
          jq -sj "${_state_args[@]}" \
             --arg sid "${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}" \
             --arg user "${USER:-unknown}" '
            def denul($z): . / $z | join("");
            def scap($z): denul($z) | sub("\n+$"; "");
            def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
            def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
                    then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
                    else 1 end;
            ([0] | implode) as $z |
            try (
              (map(.tool_name // empty | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | join("\n") | scap($z)) as $tn |
              now as $now |
              ($sid | if . == "" then $user + "-" + ($now | gmtime | strftime("%Y%m%d")) else . end) as $session |
              (if $tn == "Write"
               then (map(.tool_input.content // empty) | map(if type == "string" then slines else jl end) | add // 0)
               elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit")
               then (map(.tool_input.new_string // empty) | map(if type == "string" then slines else jl end) | add // 0)
               else 0 end) as $lines |
              (if ($tn == "Write" or $tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit")
               then (map((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end)) | join("\n") | scap($z))
               else "" end) as $file |
              (try ($state | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | fromjson)
                    | ([.[].file // empty] + [$file] | unique | length))
               catch 0) as $files_mod |
              (if $state == "" then 1 else ($state | split("\n") | length) end) as $tool_calls |
              ([$tn, ($lines | tostring), ($now | todate), ($file | tojson),
                ($session | tojson), ($files_mod | tostring), ($tool_calls | tostring)]
               | join($z) + $z)
            ) catch ("__KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__" + $z)
          ' 2>/dev/null || _jrc=$?
          printf '%s' "$_jrc"
        }
    )
    [[ "${#_kf[@]}" -ge 1 ]] || exit 0
    _jqrc="${_kf[-1]}"
    # Invalid JSON on stdin — the old `jq empty 2>/dev/null || exit 0` path.
    [[ "$_jqrc" == "0" ]] || exit 0
    # Post-validation extraction error — the old unguarded-extraction set -e
    # death (pipefail propagated jq's exit code 5).
    if [[ "${#_kf[@]}" -eq 2 && "${_kf[0]}" == "__KARPATHY_EVAL_ERR__" ]]; then
        exit 5
    fi
    [[ "${#_kf[@]}" -eq 8 ]] || exit 0  # defensive: unexpected field count

    TOOL_NAME="${_kf[0]}"
    LINES="${_kf[1]}"
    TS="${_kf[2]}"
    FILE_JSON="${_kf[3]}"
    SESSION_JSON="${_kf[4]}"
    FILES_MOD="${_kf[5]}"
    TOOL_CALLS="${_kf[6]}"
fi

[[ -n "$TOOL_NAME" ]] || exit 0

# Tool dispatch. Lines were computed for the matching shape inside jq
# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string — conservative, counts
# new content only; the v1 simplification documented in SDD §0.3).
case "$TOOL_NAME" in
    Write|Edit|NotebookEdit)
        ;;
    *)
        # Unrecognized tool — no-op (defensive: settings.json matcher should
        # prevent this, but the hook stays safe even if matcher widens).
        exit 0
        ;;
esac

[[ "$LINES" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || exit 0

# perf pass-4: skip the dirname+mkdir spawns when the parent dir already
# exists (the steady state). The guard passing proves dirname's target
# exists (e.g. "a/b" being a dir ⇒ "a" exists), so mkdir -p would be a
# no-op; every other shape (no slash, trailing slash, missing parent) takes
# the old command unchanged.
if [[ "${TASK_STATE%/*}" == "$TASK_STATE" || ! -d "${TASK_STATE%/*}" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TASK_STATE")"
fi

# Running total: sum lines_changed across existing state entries + this call.
# Awk parse is intentionally tolerant of malformed lines (skips them).
# perf pass-7: FAST serves the cached total (== the full scan's printed
# value: cache writes require an exact-decimal 15-digit integer); DELTA
# re-runs THE SAME awk program on only the token+delta bytes, seeded with
# the cached total in BEGIN — same association order as the full scan.
if [[ "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "fast" ]]; then
    RUNNING="$_kp7_bsum"
elif [[ "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "delta" ]]; then
    RUNNING=$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' -v init="$_kp7_bsum" '
        BEGIN { sum = init + 0 }
        NR == 1 { next }
        /"lines_changed":/ {
            n = $2 + 0  # extract leading integer
            sum += n
        }
        END { print sum + 0 }
    ' <(tail -c +"$_kp7_tail_from" -- "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
else
    RUNNING=$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '
        /"lines_changed":/ {
            n = $2 + 0  # extract leading integer
            sum += n
        }
        END { print sum + 0 }
    ' "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
fi
RUNNING=$((RUNNING + LINES))

# Append entry to state — printf-assembled from jq-pre-encoded pieces;
# byte-identical to the old jq -nc output (see header note).
# perf pass-7: the line is built in a variable first (printf -v cannot
# fail; identical bytes) so it can double as the cache's prefix-integrity
# token; the append keeps the old failure shape.
printf -v _kp7_entry '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s}' \
    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON"
printf '%s\n' "$_kp7_entry" >> "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# Threshold check.
if (( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )); then
    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_STATE" >&2

    # Trajectory event (#961 K-2 FR-3 schema).
    # perf pass-4: [[ -d ]] guard — mkdir -p only when the dir is missing.
    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR"
    TRAJ_FILE="$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl"
    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0

[[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0

    # A leading-zero THRESHOLD (e.g. config "007") passed the ^[0-9]+$ guard;
    # the old `jq -nc --argjson thresh "007"` PARSED it leniently and wrote
    # the decimal-normalized number (007 -> 7) — corpus-verified. Replicate
    # with a textual leading-zero strip (identical to jq's integer rendering
    # for every warn-reachable threshold).
    THRESHOLD_JSON="$THRESHOLD"
    while [[ "$THRESHOLD_JSON" == 0?* ]]; do THRESHOLD_JSON="${THRESHOLD_JSON#0}"; done

    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD_JSON" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
        >> "$TRAJ_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# perf pass-7: cache write (header note). Reached only after a successful
# append. Entirely fail-open: any guard miss skips the write and leaves the
# previous cache (stale-but-consistent: its offset still sits on a line
# boundary, so the next call simply processes a wider delta or rescans).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$_kp7_write_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then
    {
        _kp7_blen "$_kp7_entry"
        _kp7_elen="$_kp7_len"
        # Size gate (header note): small files stay on the original path
        # end-to-end — not even the post-append stat is spawned. Gated on
        # the PRE-append size + our entry (a racer pushing the true size
        # past the gate in this sliver merely delays caching one call).
        if [[ "$_kp7_elen" -ge 1 && "$_kp7_elen" -le 1024 &&
              "$RUNNING" =~ ^-?[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
              "$_kp7_s0" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
              "$((_kp7_s0 + _kp7_elen + 1))" -ge "$_KP7_MIN" ]]; then
            _kp7_post=$(stat -Lc '%d|%i|%s|%y' -- "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) || _kp7_post=""
            if [[ -n "$_kp7_post" ]]; then
                IFS='|' read -r _kp7_dev2 _kp7_ino2 _kp7_s2 _kp7_mt2 <<< "$_kp7_post"
                _kp7_wpois=""; _kp7_wnl=""; _kp7_wset=""; _kp7_wc=""
                if [[ "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "fast" || "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "delta" ]]; then
                    # Warm fold: aggregates from the warm jq + this entry.
                    # "=" = set line byte-unchanged (membership hit).
                    [[ "$_kp7_snext" == "=" ]] && _kp7_snext="$_kp7_bset"
                    if [[ "$_kp7_endsnl" == "1" && "$_kp7_allstr" == "1" &&
                          "$_kp7_pois2" =~ ^[01]$ &&
                          "$_kp7_nls" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
                          "$_kp7_wcount" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
                          "$_kp7_dlen" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ &&
                          "$_kp7_s2" == "$((_kp7_off + _kp7_dlen + _kp7_elen + 1))" ]]; then
                        _kp7_wpois="$_kp7_pois2"
                        _kp7_wnl=$((_kp7_nls + 1))
                        _kp7_wset="$_kp7_snext"
                        _kp7_wc="$_kp7_wcount"
                    fi
                elif [[ "$_kp7_s0" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
                        "$_kp7_s2" == "$((_kp7_s0 + _kp7_elen + 1))" ]]; then
                    # Cold rebuild: full-scan snapshot of the post-append
                    # file (builder guards in header note).
                    mapfile -d '' -t _kb < <(
                        { _brc=0
                          jq -nj --rawfile s "$TASK_STATE" --arg sz "$_kp7_s2" --arg tok "$_kp7_entry" '
                            ([0] | implode) as $z |
                            try (
                              (if ($s | contains("�")) then error("no") else . end) |
                              (if ($s | utf8bytelength) == ($sz | tonumber) then . else error("no") end) |
                              (if (($s | endswith("\n" + $tok + "\n")) or ($s == $tok + "\n")) then . else error("no") end) |
                              (try ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | fromjson) | [.[].file // empty]) catch null) as $fs |
                              (if $fs == null then [1, []] else [0, ($fs | unique)] end) as $pv |
                              (if ($pv[1] | all(type == "string")) then . else error("no") end) |
                              ([($pv[0] | tostring),
                                ((($s | split("\n") | length) - 1) | tostring),
                                ($pv[1] | length | tostring),
                                ($pv[1] | tojson)] | join($z) + $z)
                            ) catch ("__NO__" + $z)
                          ' 2>/dev/null || _brc=$?
                          printf '%s' "$_brc"
                        }
                    )
                    if [[ "${#_kb[@]}" -eq 5 && "${_kb[-1]}" == "0" &&
                          "${_kb[0]}" =~ ^[01]$ && "${_kb[1]}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ &&
                          "${_kb[2]}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]]; then
                        _kp7_wpois="${_kb[0]}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh — byte budgets for the always-loaded prompt surface
#
# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1). The prompt surface Claude loads on every turn or on
# every skill invocation has hard byte budgets; this is the CI gate behind them.
#
#   .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md      ≤ 16,384 B  each — charged with every
#                                  resources/*.md the skill reads UNCONDITIONALLY
#   .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      ≤ 9,445 B (cycle-129 D-3.3: min(previous cap, measured 9,189 B + 256 B); the cap never rises)
#   .claude/protocols/*.md (total) ≤ 160,000 B fail; > 114,688 B warns (reference/ is not counted)
#
# Resource charging rule (the byte budget cannot be met by moving text into a
# file the skill still always loads): a resources/<name>.md is charged when a
# SKILL.md line names it AND reads as an unguarded read imperative —
#   imperative: (?i)\b(read|load|source|include)\b          e.g. "Read `resources/X.md`"
#   guard:      (?i)\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b
# A line with a guard word ("See resources/X.md §Security", "read X.md if …") is
# a pointer, not a load, and is not charged. Pinned by tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats.
#
# Every other SKILL.md figure the sprint report needs from the "mechanical pass"
# (history tokens per file) rides along in --json as `history_tokens` —
# informational; enforcement of that rule is tests/unit/no-history-in-rule-text.bats.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh              # human table, exit 1 on any breach
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json       # machine-readable report
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root DIR   # check a fixture tree (tests / CI sentinels)
#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --quiet      # exit code only
#
# Exit codes: 0 within budget · 1 breach · 2 usage / missing root
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

ROOT="."
JSON=0
QUIET=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    --quiet|-q) QUIET=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
[[ -d "$ROOT/.claude" ]] || { echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: no .claude/ under $ROOT" >&2; exit 2; }

python3 -I - "$ROOT" "$JSON" "$QUIET" <<'PY'
import glob, json, os, re, sys
root, as_json, quiet = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] == "1", sys.argv[3] == "1"
SKILL_LIMIT, LOA_LIMIT, PROTO_FAIL, PROTO_WARN = 16384, 9445, 160000, 114688
IMPERATIVE = re.compile(r"\b(read|load|source|include)\b", re.I)
GUARD = re.compile(r"\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b", re.I)
HISTORY = re.compile(r"cycle-[0-9]{3}|#[0-9]{3,4}|KF-[0-9]{3}")
RES = re.compile(r"resources/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.md)")

def size(p):
    return os.path.getsize(p)

violations, skills = [], []
for skill_md in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, ".claude/skills/*/SKILL.md"))):
    sdir = os.path.dirname(skill_md)
    name = os.path.basename(sdir)
    charged, seen = [], set()
    text = open(skill_md, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    for ln, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        for m in RES.finditer(line):
            rel = m.group(1)
            if rel in seen or not IMPERATIVE.search(line) or GUARD.search(line):
                continue
            rp = os.path.join(sdir, "resources", rel)
            if os.path.isfile(rp):
                seen.add(rel)
                charged.append({"path": os.path.relpath(rp, root), "bytes": size(rp), "line": ln})
    total = size(skill_md) + sum(c["bytes"] for c in charged)
    ok = total <= SKILL_LIMIT
    skills.append({"skill": name, "path": os.path.relpath(skill_md, root), "skill_md_bytes": size(skill_md),
                   "charged_resources": charged, "total": total, "limit": SKILL_LIMIT, "ok": ok,
                   "history_tokens": len(HISTORY.findall(text))})
    if not ok:
        extra = f" (+{len(charged)} charged resource(s))" if charged else ""
        violations.append(f"skill {name}: {total} B > {SKILL_LIMIT} B{extra}")

loa_path = os.path.join(root, ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md")
loa = {"path": ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md", "bytes": size(loa_path) if os.path.isfile(loa_path) else 0,
       "limit": LOA_LIMIT, "present": os.path.isfile(loa_path)}
loa["ok"] = loa["bytes"] <= LOA_LIMIT
if not loa["ok"]:
    violations.append(f"CLAUDE.loa.md: {loa['bytes']} B > {LOA_LIMIT} B")

pfiles = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, ".claude/protocols/*.md")))
protos = [{"path": os.path.relpath(p, root), "bytes": size(p)} for p in pfiles]
ptotal = sum(p["bytes"] for p in protos)
protocols = {"total": ptotal, "count": len(protos), "fail_limit": PROTO_FAIL, "warn_limit": PROTO_WARN,
             "ok": ptotal <= PROTO_FAIL, "warn": PROTO_WARN < ptotal <= PROTO_FAIL, "files": protos}
if not protocols["ok"]:
    violations.append(f"protocols total: {ptotal} B > {PROTO_FAIL} B")

report = {"ok": not violations, "skills": skills, "claude_loa": loa, "protocols": protocols, "violations": violations}
if as_json:
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
elif not quiet:
    print(f"{'skill':<32}{'SKILL.md':>10}{'charged':>10}{'total':>10}  limit {SKILL_LIMIT}")
    for s in skills:
        flag = "" if s["ok"] else "  BREACH"
        print(f"{s['skill']:<32}{s['skill_md_bytes']:>10}{sum(c['bytes'] for c in s['charged_resources']):>10}{s['total']:>10}{flag}")
    print(f"CLAUDE.loa.md {loa['bytes']} B (limit {LOA_LIMIT}){'' if loa['ok'] else '  BREACH'}")
    pw = "  WARN (> %d)" % PROTO_WARN if protocols["warn"] else ("" if protocols["ok"] else "  BREACH")
    print(f"protocols total {ptotal} B over {len(protos)} files (fail > {PROTO_FAIL}){pw}")
if violations and not quiet and not as_json:
    print("\nBUDGET BREACH:", file=sys.stderr)
    for v in violations:
        print("  " + v, file=sys.stderr)
elif protocols["warn"] and not quiet and not as_json:
    print(f"WARN: protocols total {ptotal} B exceeds the {PROTO_WARN} B warning threshold", file=sys.stderr)
sys.exit(1 if violations else 0)
PY

name: Prompt Budget

# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1): the always-loaded prompt surface has hard byte
# budgets — SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read resources),
# CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,445 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn > 114,688 B).
# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh is the gate; the two sentinel steps prove the
# gate itself still bites (a scanner that exits 0 from a syntax error must not
# read as green).

on:
  # Every pull request: the gate takes seconds, and a path filter would miss the
  # shared inputs the checker charges (skill includes rendered into SKILL.md,
  # resources read unconditionally, the keep list) — Bridgebuilder F-001 on
  # PR #1266.
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  prompt-budget:
    name: Byte budgets for the prompt surface
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5

      - name: Check budgets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json > prompt-budget.json || rc=$?
          # A checker that dies before writing a report must fail LOUD with its
          # exit code, not as an opaque jq parse error (Bridgebuilder F-003).
          if ! jq -e . prompt-budget.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh --json produced no parseable report (exit $rc)"
            cat prompt-budget.json || true
            exit 1
          fi
          # Human-readable table for the log; the JSON gate below is the verdict.
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh || echo "::notice::human-readable run exited non-zero; the JSON gate decides"
          jq -r '.violations[]? | "::error::prompt budget: \(.)"' prompt-budget.json
          jq -e '.ok' prompt-budget.json >/dev/null

      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the over-budget sentinel with exit 1)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rc=0
          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over --quiet || rc=$?
          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh did not reject tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over with exit 1 (got $rc)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: over-budget sentinel rejected"

      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the under-budget sentinel)
        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under --quiet; then
            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh false-positive on tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: under-budget sentinel accepted"

      - name: Upload report

+
+These five rules govern every team. Until cycle-129 they were the C-TEAM rows of `constraints.json`, rendered into the always-loaded kernel on every turn; they now live here only (DEC-0140), because no harness surface runs on teammate spawn and the rows cost every single-agent session their bytes. The ids stay as names.
+
+| Id | Rule | Why |
+|----|------|-----|
+| C-TEAM-001 | Planning, orchestration, deployment and lifecycle skills are lead-only; teammates implement, review and audit only (the Skill Invocation Matrix below is the full list) | Planning skills produce single artifacts (PRD, SDD, sprint plan) that assume single-writer semantics; concurrent invocation would corrupt state |

# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
#
# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
#
# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.

# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.

+# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section
+# is not optional.
+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading
+  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_TABLES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r o_name o_heading <<< "$entry"
+    if [[ "$o_name" == "$section" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$o_heading"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"
+  if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file"; then
+    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local tmp="${file}.prune-tmp" rc=0
+  awk -v heading="$heading" \
+      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
+      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '
+    function flush(   i) { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print buf[i]; n = 0 }
+    state == "" && $0 == heading { state = "head"; n = 0; buf[++n] = $0; next }
+    state == "head" {
+      if (index($0, start)) { state = "skip"; n = 0; next }
+      if ($0 ~ /^\|/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) { buf[++n] = $0; next }
+      flush(); state = ""; print; next
+    }
+    state == "skip" { if (index($0, end)) state = "after"; next }
+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp" || rc=$?
+  if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    case "$rc" in
+      3) log "ERROR: ${file}: no end marker for optional section '${section}'" ;;
+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi

+          fi
+          continue
+        fi
+      fi

    33	# Counters

    39	# Utilities

    43	verbose() { [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]] && log "$@" || true; }

    47	
    48	compute_section_hash() {

    52	    | sha256_portable \
