#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
cfg() {
  local v
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
  else
    printf 'null'
  fi
}
cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi
}

_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
# previous file is untouched.
atomic_update() {
  local f="$1"; shift
  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
  (
    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
    else
      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
    fi
    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
  return $rc
}

cmd_write() {
  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
  local ts rc=0
  ts=$(now_iso)
  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
    '.schema_version = 2
     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
  local err drc=0
  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  return 0
}

bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
  local js st
  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
}

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")

    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).

    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2

    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi

#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
cmd_record_round() {
  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  local p th ts now out trip
  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
    return 0
  fi
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
        else null end ) as $trip
    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
  echo "$out"
  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
    return 10
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_mark() {
  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
    local err drc=0
    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  fi
  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
}

case "$sub" in
  write)  cmd_write ;;
  read)   cmd_read ;;
  derive) cmd_derive ;;
  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
  *) usage ;;
esac

`schema_version` 2 (cycle-125 FR-3) adds `checkpoint` — written only by
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write` (atomic, locked); `task` is the last CLOSED bead
(`null` for a phase-only checkpoint). Readers accept 1 and 2; a missing or discarded checkpoint
means sprint granularity (resume at the first open bead of `sprints.current`).

Derived cache (cycle-129 FR-5): `run-checkpoint.sh derive --write` (also run by every `write`)
rewrites `.state` (canonical) and `.status` (its mirror) from the files and adds
`"derived_at": "<ISO-8601>"` and
`"derivation": {"source": "files", "stale_markers": [], "legacy_feedback": [], "sprint_ids": []}`;
`schema_version` is kept. Files without these keys are read as before. The decision table is
in the script header; `run_mode.file_authoritative: false` makes it report-only.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)}"
SKILLS_DIR="${SKILLS_DIR:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills}"

source "$SCRIPT_DIR/yq-safe.sh"

source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/dx-utils.sh"

STRICT=false
JSON_OUTPUT=false
SINGLE_SKILL=""
AGENT_TYPES_FILE_ARG=""
unset AGENT_TYPES_FILE

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --strict) STRICT=true; shift ;;
        --json) JSON_OUTPUT=true; shift ;;
        --skill)
            # R-010 (bd-m1o6): '--skill' as the last arg used to leak a raw
            # bash '$2: unbound variable' error under set -u.
            if [[ -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
                echo "Error: --skill requires a skill name (e.g. --skill reviewing-code)" >&2
                echo "Usage: validate-skill-capabilities.sh [--strict] [--json] [--skill NAME]" >&2
                exit 2
            fi
            SINGLE_SKILL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --agent-types-file)
            if [[ -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
                echo "Error: --agent-types-file requires a path" >&2
                echo "Usage: validate-skill-capabilities.sh [--strict] [--json] [--skill NAME] [--agent-types-file PATH]" >&2
                exit 2
            fi
            AGENT_TYPES_FILE_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -h|--help)
            echo "Usage: validate-skill-capabilities.sh [--strict] [--json] [--skill NAME] [--agent-types-file PATH]"
            echo "  --strict   Promote warnings to errors"
            echo "  --json     Output as JSON"
            echo "  --skill    Validate single skill"
            echo "  --agent-types-file PATH"
            echo "             Test seam: read the write-capable agent types from PATH instead of"
            echo "             .claude/data/agent-types.yaml (the AGENT_TYPES_FILE variable is ignored)"
            exit 0
            ;;
        *)
            dx_unknown_flag "$1" "Usage: validate-skill-capabilities.sh [--strict] [--json] [--skill NAME] [--agent-types-file PATH]" \
                --strict --json --skill --agent-types-file --help
            exit 2
            ;;
    esac
done

The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. +- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.

     3	# implement-gate.sh — Dual-mode compliance hook for App Zone writes (FR-7)
     4	# =============================================================================

     6	# /implement or /bug skill invocation.
     7	#
     8	# Modes (cycle-129 D-4.1, DEC-0163; .loa.config.yaml implement_gate.mode):
     9	#   ask (default; unset or any other value): an unsanctioned App-Zone write asks,
    10	#       exactly as before, and now logs one row (decision "ask").
    11	#   telemetry: an unsanctioned App-Zone write logs one row (action "telemetry",
    12	#       decision "outside_run") and is allowed silently.
    13	#   deny: an unsanctioned App-Zone write is DENIED when the run position is
    14	#       known: .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and its derived_at is within
    15	#       run_mode.stale_hours (12). The gate is a fence only in this mode. An
    16	#       unknown position (cache missing, not derived, stale or unparseable)
    17	#       falls back to ask (decision "unknown_position"), never to allow.
    18	# Sanction (any mode; first match wins; one row each, action "allow"):
    19	#   sanctioned_run    — the heuristic below: a fresh RUNNING cache, and its
    20	#                       derived_at (when present) within run_mode.stale_hours
    21	#   sanctioned_marker — .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint,
    22	#                       started_at} with started_at within two hours (written by
    23	#                       `run-checkpoint.sh mark`, removed by `unmark`); a stale or
    24	#                       malformed marker logs decision "stale_marker" and does not sanction
    25	#   override          — LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the hook's environment
    26	# Rows go to .run/audit.jsonl as {ts, hook: "implement-gate", action, decision,
    27	# mode, path} with path control-stripped and cut to 256 bytes; LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    28	# adds replay: true to every row this gate writes (DEC-0167).
    29	#
    30	# Claims modifier (implement_gate.claims: authoritative; the legacy
    31	# implement_gate.mode: authoritative means mode ask + claims authoritative):
    32	#   reads tool_input.active_skill from hook stdin. The PreToolUse
    33	#      payload carries no harness-set skill field (cycle-126 D-4.4) and tool_input
    34	#      is model-authored, so nothing in .run/ selects this modifier.
    35	#      TIGHTEN-ONLY (sprint-250 audit n17/n18): the model-authored claim can only
    36	#      add an ask, never grant an allow. A claimed implementation skill falls
    37	#      through to the heuristic exactly like an absent field; a claimed
    38	#      non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny with a known position and no
    39	#      sanction, is denied) and logs compliance.mode.model_signal to
    40	#      .run/audit.jsonl (plain hook log, not the signed audit_emit chain). Every
    41	#      claim leaves one row per invocation: decision "ask"/"deny" for a non-implementation
    42	#      claim, decision "heuristic" for an implementation claim (run-2 finding 6).
    43	#
    44	# `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode [CONFIG]` prints the effective mode (and the
    45	# claims modifier) without reading stdin — the /loa Gate line.
    46	#
    47	# Evidence recorder (cycle-126 D-4.4): a lead-session payload carrying
    48	# tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at once in
    49	# .run/platform-features.json. It is evidence only and never changes the mode.

    53	# findings 1/5). The path is tool_input.file_path, or tool_input.notebook_path for
    54	# NotebookEdit; a relative path resolves from the payload's cwd, else PROJECT_ROOT
    55	# (run-3 finding 6). The zone test ORs a physical form (symlinks followed) and a
    56	# logical form (symlinks kept) and matches a lowercased copy (run-3 findings 1/2).
    57	# Root: PROJECT_ROOT, else CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else this script's location

    59	# Claude's `cd` (audit MED-001); RUN_DIR defaults to <root>/.run.
    60	# Trust inputs: a write to .run/state.json, .run/sprint-plan-state.json,
    61	# .run/simstim-state.json, .run/platform-features.json, .run/audit.jsonl,
    62	# .run/implement-active.json or .loa.config.yaml asks in every mode and under

   104	# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
   105	# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,

   107	# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
   108	# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
   109	_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
   110	_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
   111	    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
   112	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
   113	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   114	    done
   115	    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
   116	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   117	    done
   118	    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
   119	        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   120	    done
   121	    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
   122	        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   123	    done

   125	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   126	    done
   127	    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
   128	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   129	    done
   130	    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
   131	        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
   132	    done

   135	# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte

   137	# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row

   139	    local LC_ALL=C
   140	    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
   141	    _c_n=${#_c_s}
   142	    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
   143	        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
   144	        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
   145	        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
   146	        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
   147	        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
   148	        fi

#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
       notes: ([
         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
       ]),
       sprints: $f.sprints,
       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,

content.text:
I found six defects in the profiles area. Each one was reproduced in a scratch copy under /tmp.

Test run: `tests/unit/profile-lib.bats` passes 15 of 17. I had to add a stand-in `floor.yaml`, because `.claude/data/floor.yaml` is not in the PR tree. PL-14 and PL-15 fail only because files outside the PR tree are missing (for example `time-lib.sh`). I ran the Profile line function on its own and it printed the expected output. I could not run `profile-floor.bats`: it needs `floor.yaml`, `compat-lib.sh`, `verdict-derive.sh` and the adversarial gate, none of which are in the PR tree.

### Findings

**1. The cache goes stale whenever one of its three input files is missing (Linux / GNU stat)** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77-78` — confidence: high
- `stat -Lc` exits non-zero if any of the three files (config, profiles, floor) is missing, even though it printed lines for the files that exist. That triggers the BSD fallback, `stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z'`.
- On GNU, `-f` means filesystem status. So the cache key is built from disk-wide figures (free blocks and so on), with no file mtime or size, and the good output from the first `stat` is thrown away.
- The comment at lines 73-74 says the key has "one stat line per existing file", which is not what happens.
- Repro 1: no `floor.yaml`. Alternating `loa.profile: lean` and `full` in the config, `profile` printed `full full` five times in a row.
- Repro 2: `floor.yaml` present but no `.loa.config.yaml` (a fresh install). After editing `profiles.yaml`, `knob soul_identity_doc.enabled` kept returning the old `false` until I deleted `.run/`.

**2. The shipped example makes the profile knob almost inert** — `pr/head/.loa.config.yaml.example:21` (also lines 313, 326, 1354, 1358, 1404) — confidence: high
- The example explicitly sets 8 of the 9 profile keys. Explicit keys win, so a user who copies it and changes `loa.profile` sees only `soul_identity_doc.enabled` change.
- I resolved the example with `loa.profile: full`: guardrails, the KF and decisions surfaces, and `structured_handoff` all stayed `false`. `overrides` listed 5 keys.
- This contradicts the example's own text: line 21 says "`lean` turns them all off, `full` all on", and line 1354 says "`full` turns them on" directly above `enabled: false` (line 1358) and `enforce: false` (line 1404).
- PL-4 only checks that example equals standard, so it cannot catch this.

**3. Without jq, the KF and decisions hooks now go silent even when explicitly enabled** — `pr/head/.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh:63-64` and `pr/head/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh:50-51` — confidence: high
- `loa_knob` needs both jq and yq (profile-lib.sh lines 188 and 208). Without jq it returns the fallback `false`, even when the config says `true`.
- Base behaviour with yq but no jq, and `surface_at_session_start: true`:
  - The decisions hook printed `[DECISIONS] WARNING: ... jq is missing`.
  - The KF hook (which does not need jq at all) printed its degraded WARNING.
- Head behaviour: both print nothing and exit 0.
- That breaks each hook's documented contract: decisions hook lines 11-12 ("Enabled but ... jq is missing → one WARNING line"; the warning at line 66 can no longer be reached when yq is present) and KF hook line 25 ("never silent on an enabled-but-broken path").
- The L7 soul hook (lines 69-73) picks up the same new jq dependency.

**4. The floor check misses an ancestor of a wildcard floor key, and any descendant** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:124` — confidence: medium
- `forbidden()` only tests whether the key starts with the text before the first `*`.
- With floor keys `flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice` and `hounfour.locality`, the profile keys `flatline_protocol.code_review` and `hounfour.locality.mode` were accepted into `profile_keys` with no WARN.
- The header (line 37) promises "an ancestor of a floor key also counts".
- `tests/unit/profile-floor.bats:56-57` (PF-2) copies the same logic, so it cannot detect the gap.
- Practical impact needs an edit to `profiles.yaml` plus a reader that calls `loa_knob` on such a key; no such reader exists today.

**5. The lib's test seams work in production, unlike every other hook seam** — `pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:51,61-64` — confidence: medium
- `LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILES_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE`, `LOA_PROFILE_ROOT` and `LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE` are honoured without a bats check. Only `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE` is gated.
- The KF, decisions and L7 hooks deliberately gate their config overrides on bats plus an opt-in flag (L7 cites the "CRIT-1 remediation").
- Now one environment variable redirects their enable flags, and also `guardrails.danger_level.enforce` / `guardrails.input.enabled` in `danger-level-enforcer.sh:141` and `guardrails-orchestrator.sh:110`, to any file. `LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE=/dev/null` switches the floor filter off.

**6. The run-mode guardrails reader was not converted** — `pr/head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:26` — confidence: medium
- It still says "Skip ... when `.loa.config.yaml` has `guardrails.input.enabled: false`", so when the key is absent the guardrails run.
- Every other skill and the shared include now use `profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false`, where standard means off.
- `tools/check-knob-readers.sh` skips it by design because it only flags dotted `.key` forms. So "every profile key is read through loa_knob" does not hold.

### Lower confidence (behaviour changes, possibly intended)
- **`invisible_retrospective.enabled` flips on for existing configs without the key** — `pr/head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42`, `pr/head/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json:56-62`. The old reader ran only on an explicit `true` (empty config and this repo: `false`). Standard is now `true`. This repo's `.loa.config.yaml` has no such key, so the retrospective now runs here. Unlike the guardrail keys, the oracle and the profiles header do not call this out as a migration item. Confidence: low-medium.
- **Inconsistent fallback** — `pr/head/.claude/skills/continuous-learning/resources/retrospective-postlude.md:34` uses fallback `true`, but the generated include (`.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1`) passes no fallback, which means empty, i.e. off. Harmless while the lib resolves. Confidence: low.

All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

Separate counter from the main circuit breaker (see `resources/conditional-procedures.md`
§red-team-code-gate for behavior).

+++ b/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md
@@ -70,6 +70,20 @@ ## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)
 fence territory (`block-destructive-bash.sh` and the System-Zone rules), not
 frontmatter territory.
 
+**What the harness enforces (live probe, cycle-129 Sprint 2, Claude Code 2.1.296).**
+In the main session, invoking a skill that carries `disallowed-tools: Write, Edit,
+NotebookEdit` removed the three tools until the next user prompt — the next Write
+was refused ("Permission to use Write has been denied"), later calls reported the
+tools "disabled for this session, in subagents as well", and invoking a write-capable
+skill did not restore them; in an unattended run that is the rest of the session
+(KF-043). A Bash redirect still wrote a file (the Bash gap above). In a subagent
+(`general-purpose`, all tools) the same skill removed nothing: Write, Edit and Bash
+all succeeded, and `allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob` did not restrict either. So the
+key is a barrier in the main session only; for subagent work the zones, the fence and
+the implement gate are the barriers. Keep the key (it holds where the review and audit
+skills run) and never invoke such a skill from a lead session that still has writes
+to do.
+

+# × sanction {none, run_fresh, run_stale, marker_fresh, marker_stale, override}
+# × cache {fresh, stale, missing, unparseable} (run_* sanctions define the cache themselves)

+# $1 mode (unset = no key) $2 claims (plain | authoritative)

+    fi
+    return 0

+# $1 cache: fresh | stale | missing | unparseable | run_fresh | run_stale (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
+cache_state() {
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    case "$1" in
+        missing) ;;
+        unparseable) printf '{"state": "RUNNING", \n' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        fresh)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        stale)     jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", status: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_fresh) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;
+        run_stale) jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "RUNNING", status: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 13 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json" ;;

+
+# $1 sanction: none | marker_fresh | marker_stale | override (run_* handled by cache_state); echoes the override value
+marker_state() {

+gate_cell() {

+# The expected "<decision> <row>" for one cell; row = action/decision of the write's decision row

+    local mode="$1" claims="$2" wclass="$3" sanction="$4" cache="$5" sanctioned=0 known=0
+    [[ "$mode" == unset ]] && mode=ask
+    if [[ "$wclass" == trust ]]; then echo "ask ask/trust_input"; return; fi
+    case "$sanction" in run_fresh|marker_fresh|override) sanctioned=1 ;; esac

+        telemetry) echo "allow telemetry/outside_run" ;;
+        deny) if (( known )); then echo "deny deny/deny"; else echo "ask ask/unknown_position"; fi ;;

+                    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$cell: exit $status" >&2; return 1; }
+                    want=$(expect_cell "$mode" "$claims" "$wclass" "$sanction" "$cache")
+                    got="$(decision3)"
+                    [ "$got" = "${want%% *}" ] || { echo "$cell: expected ${want%% *}, got $got" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # the write's decision row: the claim row (model_signal), the trust row (state_write) or the gate row
+                    row=$(jq -sr 'map(select(.action != "note" and (.hook == "implement-gate"))) | if length == 1 then "\(.[0].action)/\(.[0].decision)" else "count:\(length)" end' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null) || row="no-rows"

+                    else

+                    fi
+                    # every row this gate wrote carries replay: true under LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 (DEC-0167)
+                    n=$(jq -s 'map(select(.replay != true)) | length' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl")
+                    [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "$cell: $n rows without replay: true" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # telemetry prints nothing at all
+                    if [[ "${want#* }" == telemetry/outside_run ]]; then
+                        [[ -z "$output" && -z "$stderr" ]] || { echo "$cell: telemetry printed something" >&2; return 1; }
+                    fi
+                done
+            done
+        done
+    done

content.content:
# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
# =============================================================================

_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
_LOA_PL_JSON=""
_LOA_PL_ID=""

_loa_pl_paths() {
  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
  else
    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
  fi
}

# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
_loa_pl_id() {
  local st
  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    return 0
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
}

_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
_loa_pl_build() {
  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
      cfg='{}'
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
      prof='{}'
    fi
  else
    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
  fi
  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";

# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
# =============================================================================

_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
_LOA_PL_JSON=""
_LOA_PL_ID=""

_loa_pl_paths() {
  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
  else
    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
  fi
}

# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
_loa_pl_id() {
  local st
  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    return 0
  fi
  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
}

_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
_loa_pl_build() {
  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
      cfg='{}'
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
      prof='{}'
    fi
  else
    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
  fi
  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
  fi
  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;

    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |

### Task Tracking: Beads vs TaskCreate

Use `br` (beads_rust) exclusively for sprint task lifecycle (commands below). Claude's `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` are for session-level progress display only; tasks tracked only there are invisible to cross-session recovery, `/run-resume`, and beads health checks.

```bash
health=$(.claude/scripts/beads/beads-health.sh --quick --json)
status=$(echo "$health" | jq -r '.status')
```

`HEALTHY` → import state (`br sync --import-only`; `update-beads-state.sh --sync-import`) and proceed. `DEGRADED` → warn, import, proceed. `NOT_INSTALLED`/`NOT_INITIALIZED` → check opt-out (`update-beads-state.sh --opt-out-check`); without one, warn (`cargo install beads_rust && br init` to add it) and fall back to markdown. `MIGRATION_NEEDED`/`UNHEALTHY` → warn, fall back to markdown. Record the outcome: `.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh --health "$status"`.

Run the full lifecycle per task yourself: health check → `br sync --import-only` → `.claude/scripts/beads/get-ready-work.sh` (not bare `br ready`) → `br update <id> --status in_progress` → implement → `br close <id>` (run mode: then `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --task <id> --phase IMPLEMENT`) → `br sync --flush-only` at session end. Log discovered issues as they surface — this adds a `discovered-during:<parent-id>` label for traceability:

```bash
.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh "$CURRENT_TASK_ID" "Description of discovered issue" bug 2
```

bootstrap_section() {
  local file="$1"
  local section="$2"
  local content="$3"

  local hash
  hash=$(compute_section_hash "$content")

  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

  if grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section}" "$file"; then
    verbose "Section ${section} already has markers in ${file}, skipping bootstrap"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find anchor for this section
  local anchor_start="" anchor_end=""
  for anchor in "${ANCHORS[@]}"; do
    local a_section a_start a_end
    IFS='|' read -r a_section a_start a_end <<< "$anchor"
    if [[ "$a_section" == "$section" ]]; then
      anchor_start="$a_start"
      anchor_end="$a_end"
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ -z "$anchor_start" ]]; then
    log "WARNING: No anchor defined for section ${section}, skipping"
    return 0
  fi

  # For skill-md sections, use <constraints> tags
  if [[ "$anchor_start" == *"SKILL_ANCHOR"* ]]; then
    verbose "Skill section ${section}: markers will be inserted inside <constraints> block during generation"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find the anchor line and insert markers after the table header
  local matches
  matches=$(grep -c "$anchor_start" "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [[ "$matches" -ne 1 ]]; then
    log "ERROR: Anchor '${anchor_start}' matches ${matches} times in ${file} (expected 1)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Find the section: locate header, keep table header+separator, wrap data rows with markers
  local tmp="${file}.bootstrap-tmp"
  local end_pat1="${anchor_end%%|*}"
  local end_pat2="${anchor_end#*|}"
  awk -v anchor="$anchor_start" \
      -v end_pat1="$end_pat1" \
      -v end_pat2="$end_pat2" \
      -v start_m="$start_marker" \
      -v warning_m="$warning" \
      -v end_m="$end_marker" \
      -v content_m="$content" \
      '
      BEGIN { state="looking"; sep_seen=0 }
      state == "looking" && $0 ~ anchor {
        print; state="in_header"; next
      }
      state == "in_header" {
        # Print everything until we see the separator row (|---|)
        print
        if ($0 ~ /^\|[-|: ]+\|$/) {
          sep_seen=1
          print start_m
          print warning_m
          printf "%s\n", content_m
          state="skipping"
        }
        next
      }
      state == "skipping" {
        if ($0 ~ end_pat1 || $0 ~ end_pat2) {
          print end_m
          if ($0 !~ /^$/) print
          state="done"
          next
        }
        # Skip original data rows (replaced by generated content)
        next
      }
      state != "skipping" { print }
      END {
        if (state == "skipping") print end_m
      }
      ' "$file" > "$tmp"

  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    diff -u "$file" "$tmp" || true
    rm -f "$tmp"
  else
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    log "Bootstrapped markers for section '${section}' in ${file}"
  fi
}

content.text:
I found seven defects in `run-checkpoint.sh`, its run-mode docs and its tests. The record-round tests (RCR-1..8) and RCD-1..17 pass, but only with jq 1.7.1. With the system jq 1.6, almost every derive test fails (finding 4).

How I ran them: `verdict-derive.sh` is not part of the PR snapshot, so I ran under a scratch copy in `/tmp/rcw` with a stub version of it. RCD-R1..R5 could not run because they call scripts that are also missing from the snapshot (`loa-run-state-surface.sh`, `run-preflight.sh`, `golden-path.sh`, the implement-gate hook, `loa-status.sh`).

### Findings

1. **`derive --write` creates a broken circuit breaker when none exists.** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:295` (with `:154` and `:456`). Confidence: high.
   - When the breaker file is absent, `atomic_update` feeds `{}` to jq (line 154). `merge_breaker` only falls back to the skeleton when the input is not an object (`if type == "object" then . else skeleton(...)`), and `{}` is an object.
   - Reproduced result: `{"triggers":{"cycle_count":{"current":0}},"state":"CLOSED"}`. It has no thresholds, no limits, no `timeout.started` and no `history`.
   - The `--json` path (where `bcache` is `null`) does get the skeleton, so the report and the written file disagree.
   - Afterwards `record-round` keeps this object, because its own check at line 496 only asks for `.triggers` to be an object. It then prints `cycle 2/null, same_issue 2/null, no_progress 1/null`, and the **timeout trigger can never fire** (`$start` is null).
   - Any `write` or `mark` before the run creates its breaker triggers this. Fix: use `(.triggers|type)=="object"` at line 295, as record-round does.

2. **`write --file F` outside a `.run/` dir derives against this checkout and writes its breaker.** Lines 109-117 and 174. Confidence: high.
   - Root and run dir fall back to the script's checkout. The automatic `derive --write` then reads the checkout's ledger, rewrites F's `.state`/`.status`/`derivation` from it, and creates or updates `<checkout>/.run/circuit-breaker.json`.
   - Reproduced: F `/tmp/rcw/other/sp.json` went from state COMPLETE to RUNNING using the checkout ledger, and the checkout's `.run/circuit-breaker.json` was created.
   - If the checkout has no `.run/`, a raw bash error about the `.lock` redirection leaks to stderr instead.
   - Base `write --file` never touched anything but F, so this is a regression for any caller or test that uses a temp `--file`.

3. **`read` regression from the new `set -e`.** Line 78, together with lines 191 and 197. Confidence: high.
   - A file that parses but has the wrong shape now aborts with jq's exit 5. Examples: `{"schema_version":2,"checkpoint":"abc"}`, or a top-level array.
   - The header contract (line 19) says "Exit 0 always when F exists". Base printed "malformed checkpoint" / "sprint granularity" and exited 0; I confirmed both behaviours side by side.

4. **`derive` is broken on jq 1.6.** Confidence: medium (depends on which jq versions are supported). I found no stated minimum jq version in the files I searched (`base/`, `head/`). jq 1.6 is the default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04.
   - Lines 378-380 and 389: `--arg label` / `$label` is a jq ≤1.6 keyword, so the expression fails to compile ("unexpected label"). Every derive call then fails, and inside `write`/`mark` it is swallowed with a misleading "is not valid JSON — not written" message.
   - Lines 223 and 226: `jq -e 'type=="object'` on empty input exits 0 in 1.6. For a trailer-less (legacy) feedback file `pj` stays empty, `--argjson p ''` fails, and `fb_parse` breaks both record-round and derive on legacy files.
   - Renaming the variable to `$lbl` and adding a `[[ -n "$pj" ]]` guard makes all 25 runnable tests pass on jq 1.6.

5. **Doc contradicts code in halt-resume step 0a.** `head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:49-52`. Confidence: medium.
   - The doc says `derive --write` makes "the steps below read the file-derived position".
   - The steps below read `.run/state.json` (and the breaker). `derive` never writes `.run/state.json`; it only writes `sprint-plan-state.json` and the breaker.
   - For a single-sprint run (no `sprint-plan-state.json`), `derive --write` writes nothing at all.

6. **`--reset-ice` does not clear `triggers.no_progress.last_counts`, a field this PR adds.** `head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:81`, used by `run-checkpoint.sh:501`. Confidence: medium.
   - After a reset, the first `record-round` with the same counts as the last pre-reset round gets `no_progress` 1 instead of 0. I reproduced this.
   - That contradicts the documented intent that "rounds before [reset_at] no longer count" (state-schemas.md, halt-resume.md). It also disagrees with derive's recompute, which gives 0.

7. **RCR-5 does not test what its name claims.** `head/tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats:105`. Confidence: medium.
   - The title says the triggers "trip in that documented order", but each of its three cases satisfies exactly one trigger. Precedence (for example no_progress over cycle_count) is never exercised.
   - The listed order (cycle, no-progress, timeout) also differs from the documented one (same_issue, no_progress, cycle_count, timeout).

All reproduction scripts are in `/tmp/rcw` (`mkfix.sh` builds the fixture; `repo16/` is the copy patched for jq 1.6). Nothing under `/workspace/pr` was modified.

content.text:
I found three defects I'd stand behind (two high, one medium) and four lower-confidence issues. All are in `karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh` and `implement-gate.sh`, plus one weak test. I checked each one by reading the code and, where it says so, by running a scenario against copies in `~/scratch/`; nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Test runs.** The snapshot is incomplete, so I had to patch the copies before anything ran:
- Mode bits were lost, and `/tmp` won't execute files, so I ran from `~/scratch` with `chmod +x`.
- Line 165 of `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats` and line 141 of `karpathy-surgical-diff-hook.bats` are a scrubbing artifact (`local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"`). It is in base too and doesn't count as a PR defect, but it stops the file parsing, so I fixed it in the copies.

After that, all 11 tests in `karpathy-surgical-diff.bats` and all 6 in `karpathy-surgical-diff-hook.bats` pass. In `implement-gate.bats`, the new tests IG-14 through IG-33 pass; IG-1 to IG-10, IG-12 and IG-14 fail only because fixtures and scripts aren't in the snapshot (`pretooluse-payloads/`, `detect-platform-features.sh`). `karpathy-trajectory-event.bats` skips because its schema isn't in the snapshot, and `guard-yield.bats` and `golden-path-c8-verdict-trailer.bats` can't run because `guard-yield.sh` and `bootstrap.sh` are missing.

## Findings

**1. The per-task counter is filed under the wrong task (one task behind). Confidence: high.**
`head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:132` keys on `.checkpoint.task`, and the header (lines 10–11) calls that "the current task".
- The checkpoint actually records the last *closed* task, per `head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/state-schemas.md:107`. `implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:211` only writes it after `br close <id>`. `run-checkpoint.sh read` (around line 199) also drops any task that is still open.
- So lines written while working on task B are stored in `A.jsonl` and the summary says `task: A`. Task A's own lines went to `sprint-N.jsonl`, because the sprint-start checkpoint has no task.
- `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:220` tells the reviewer to read `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` for each sprint bead, so it reads the next task's diff.
- Test KS-1 (`tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:54`) builds exactly this setup, with the task marked closed, and asserts the shifted label, so it can't catch the bug.

**2. A finished run never lets go of the counter, which brings back the unbounded session-long total. Confidence: high.**
`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:129-137` uses whatever `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` returns and never checks that `.state` is RUNNING.
- A run that has ended (JACKED_OUT, COMPLETE or HALTED) leaves `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` and its checkpoint behind.
- From then on, every Write or Edit in every later session goes into the same `sprint-N.jsonl`, or into the last task's file when `br` confirms it closed.
- The documented fallback ("with no run in progress the key is the session id", header line 12 and KS-2 at bats line 70) never applies.
- Verified: with a JACKED_OUT state file, three different `session_id`s all went into `state/sprint-9.jsonl`, the total reached 9 and the warning fired on every write after that.
- The same thing happens without `br`: every task checkpoint is thrown away, so a whole sprint shares one counter.

**3. Under `implement_gate.mode: deny`, a direct `/implement` that runs past 2 hours gets hard-denied. Confidence: medium.**
In `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh` the marker counts for 2 hours (line 550, `_ig_within 7200`), but the run position counts as known for `stale_hours`, 12 hours by default (line 564).
- `run-checkpoint.sh mark` writes the marker once and also runs `derive --write`, which refreshes `derived_at` whenever a `sprint-plan-state.json` exists, for example one left by an earlier run.
- Between hour 2 and hour 12 of an `/implement` session, App-Zone writes go through lines 628–633 and are **denied** instead of falling back to ask.
- The deny message then tells the user to "run /implement or /bug", which is what they are already doing.
- Nothing in `implementing-tasks` or `bug-triaging` refreshes the marker.
- Verified: marker 2.5 hours old, fresh `derived_at`, state JACKED_OUT gives `permissionDecision: "deny"`.

**4. The docs list the audit `action` values incompletely. Confidence: low–medium.**
`implement-gate.sh:593` writes an extra row with `action: "note"` and `decision: stale_marker`. `head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:271` says the action is one of allow, ask, telemetry or deny, and the header says one row per decision. The test matrix already filters out `action != "note"`.

    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then

head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:546 — Per-segment body scan only keeps segments whose first word is a fence verb, and _bdb_hd_segword does not strip shell keywords (then/do/else/{ after split, function bodies `x() { rm …`), so `if true; then rm -rf src; fi` in a nonexec heredoc body is dropped. Combined with the line-612 gap this is an allow-regression vs base (base blocks): `cat <<'EOF' > notes.md` / `if true; then rm -rf src; fi` / `EOF` / `bash note*` exits 0 — the "fail-closed" classifier is not fail-closed.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:612 — _bdb_hd_same_line_exec only detects later execution when the target's literal basename appears on another line; a glob (`bash note*`, `sh n.tx?`) or substitution (`bash "$(ls notes*)"`) on a later line of the same command executes the heredoc target undetected (verified rc=0 in head, rc=2 in base).
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:592 — The variable-command-word synthesis (`$x -rf src` also scanned as rm/git/kubectl) is inert: the FR-2 rm gate at line 2223 (and the git/kubectl pre-filters) test the raw $command for the literal "rm"/"git", not $_cmd_match, so the synthetic lines are never evaluated unless the original text already contains the word. `cat <<EOF > notes.md\n$x -rf src\nEOF` and `x=1; $x -rf src` are allowed; D136 only passes because `x=rm` contains "rm".
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:732 — Comment (and .loa.config.yaml.example:1243) claim "turning it off only tightens", but heredoc_classifier: false restores the #1245 scrub, which ALLOWS D122 (`cat > cleanup.sh <<'EOF' rm -rf src`) and D123 (shebang body) that the classifier blocks (verified with run-corpus.sh --knob-off). The rollback key loosens the fence; the docs mislead operators.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh:5 — The library is introduced for guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic, but guard-yield.sh is not touched by this PR, so nothing sources the library and the guard-yield.bats row change (tests/unit/guard-yield.bats:34) asserts behaviour attributed to a classifier the script under test never calls — an inert control added in a sprint about retiring inert controls.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:78 — Cache key: GNU `stat -Lc` exits 1 when any of config/profiles/floor is missing (e.g. a fresh install with no .loa.config.yaml), so the `stat -Lf` BSD fallback runs; on GNU `-f` prints filesystem stats (no mtime/size), so the cache key never changes and edits to profiles.yaml/.loa.config.yaml are ignored until .run/effective-config.json is deleted (reproduced: alternating lean/full kept returning the stale profile).
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:21 — The shipped example explicitly sets 8 of the 9 profile-governed keys (also lines 313, 326, 1354/1358, 1404), and explicit keys win, so a user copying it and switching loa.profile to lean/full changes only soul_identity_doc.enabled — contradicting the example's own "lean turns them all off, full all on" text; the profile knob is effectively inert for anyone starting from the example.
head/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh:50 — Enable flag now read via loa_knob, which needs jq AND yq and returns the fallback false when jq is absent; an explicitly enabled surface with jq missing now exits silently instead of printing the documented "enabled but jq is missing" WARNING (the warning branch at line 66 is unreachable). Same regression in head/.claude/hooks/loa-kf-surface.sh:63 (contract "never silent on an enabled-but-broken path"; KF never needed jq before) and the L7 soul hook.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:124 — forbidden() only checks a glob match or whether the floor key's pre-`*` prefix starts with `<key>.`; ancestors of a wildcard floor key (`flatline_protocol.code_review` vs `flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice`) and descendants of a floor key (`hounfour.locality.mode` vs `hounfour.locality`) pass, contrary to the header's "an ancestor of a floor key also counts" — a profile can reach under the floor. PF-2 (tests/unit/profile-floor.bats:56) copies the same logic so cannot catch it.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:61 — LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE / LOA_PROFILES_FILE / LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE / LOA_PROFILE_ROOT are honoured in production (only LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is bats-gated), so a single env var redirects guardrails.danger_level.enforce, guardrails.input.enabled and the session-start enable flags to an arbitrary file, and LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE=/dev/null disables the floor — undoing the bats-gated seam discipline (CRIT-1) those hooks had.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:26 — Still gates input guardrails on `.loa.config.yaml` having `guardrails.input.enabled: false` (absent ⇒ run), while every other reader now uses `profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` (standard ⇒ off); the run-mode reader was not converted and tools/check-knob-readers.sh cannot see it.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:295 — merge_breaker falls back to the skeleton only when the input is not an object, but atomic_update (line 154) feeds `{}` when circuit-breaker.json is absent; `derive --write` therefore writes a breaker with no thresholds/limits/timeout.started/history (`{"triggers":{"cycle_count":{"current":0}},"state":"CLOSED"}`), record-round keeps it, reports `cycle 2/null`, and the timeout trigger can never fire. The --json path uses the skeleton, so report and file disagree.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:113 — `write --file F` with F outside a `.run/` directory leaves root/run_dir at this checkout, so the automatic derive --write rewrites F's state/status from the checkout's ledger and creates/updates <checkout>/.run/circuit-breaker.json (base only touched F); with no .run/ a raw bash lock-redirect error leaks.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:78 — New `set -e` makes cmd_read abort with jq exit 5 on a file that parses but has the wrong shape (`{"schema_version":2,"checkpoint":"abc"}`, top-level array) at line 197, breaking the documented "Exit 0 always when F exists" contract (base printed malformed checkpoint and exited 0).
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378 — derive uses `--arg label` / `$label`, a reserved keyword in jq ≤1.6 (compile error "unexpected label"), so every derive (and the derive inside write/mark, surfaced as a misleading "not valid JSON — not written") fails on jq 1.6 (Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 default); also lines 223/226 rely on `jq -e` failing on empty input, which jq 1.6 does not, breaking fb_parse on trailer-less feedback.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:49 — Step 0a says `derive --write` makes the following steps read the file-derived position, but those steps read .run/state.json, which derive never writes (it only writes sprint-plan-state.json and the breaker; for a single-sprint run it writes nothing).
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:81 — --reset-ice does not clear triggers.no_progress.last_counts (new in this PR, used at run-checkpoint.sh:501), so the first post-reset record-round with unchanged counts gets no_progress=1, contradicting "rounds before reset_at no longer count" and derive's recompute (0).
head/tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats:105 — RCR-5 claims the triggers "trip in that documented order" but each case satisfies exactly one trigger, so precedence is never exercised; its listed order also differs from the documented order (same_issue, no_progress, cycle_count, timeout).
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:132 — The per-task key uses .checkpoint.task, which records the last CLOSED task (state-schemas.md:107; written after `br close`), so lines written for task B are filed under A.jsonl and labelled task A, and reviewing-code/SKILL.md:220 sends the reviewer to the wrong task's diff; KS-1 (tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats:54) asserts the shifted label.
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:129 — Uses whatever `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` returns without checking the run is RUNNING; a finished (COMPLETE/JACKED_OUT/HALTED) run's leftover sprint-plan-state.json makes every later session accumulate into the same sprint-N.jsonl, reintroducing the unbounded cross-session total and making the documented session-id fallback unreachable (verified with three session ids → one counter, warning on every write).
head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:564 — Under mode deny, the /implement marker is honoured for 2 h (line 550) but the run position counts as known for stale_hours (12 h), which mark/derive --write refresh; a direct /implement longer than 2 h is hard-denied (lines 628–633) instead of asking, with a message telling the user to run /implement — which they are doing.
head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:271 — Documents implement-gate audit `action` as one of allow/ask/telemetry/deny with one row per decision, but implement-gate.sh:593 also writes an `action: "note"` / `decision: stale_marker` row.
head/tests/unit/golden-path-c8-verdict-trailer.bats:452 — The doc-lock greps run-checkpoint.sh for `verdict-derive.sh --json` and `no trailer`, which occur only in the header comment; the code invokes `bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" … --json`, so the test passes regardless of the implementation.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
